idiom_name: express cookie-session middleware (base64 JSON signed with Keygrip keys) or a signed JWT in a cookie
implementation_notes: Node itself has no session facility - req and res are plain objects - so the realization is middleware: cookie-session keeps the whole session object in one cookie by JSON-encoding it to base64 and signing it with a Keygrip key list (keys: new Keygrip([...], 'SHA384', 'base64')), which provides tamper detection and key rotation but no confidentiality, because the payload is only encoded. Configure name, httpOnly, secure, sameSite and maxAge at the middleware, and remember the documented guidance: when the session grows toward the roughly 4 KB cookie limit or holds anything sensitive, move the data to a server-side store or an encrypted-cookie/JWT library instead. The hand-written form (base64 + crypto.createHmac plus manual Set-Cookie headers) is only worth it when the session must travel in a custom header or a non-standard carrier.
pitfalls: Signed is not encrypted: the session object is base64 JSON that any client can read, so secrets and PII must not go in it.
Everything stored is re-sent on every request and the browser rejects oversized cookies (Express's own documentation points at a server-side store once this bites).
The Keygrip list must be ordered current key first and kept in secret storage; a wrong order or a rotated key signs every live session out.
Two parallel requests each carry their own copy of the session, so the last response wins and an XHR can overwrite a navigation's update.
